userStories.description:
# F2 · Core UI primitives

**Foundation ticket — land right after F1.** Every screen currently re-implements the same button/input/card/pill inline with copy-pasted class strings and repeated `min-h-[44px]` magic numbers. Extract them into a small set of primitives so the whole app is consistent and SOL only styles each pattern once.

Create `src/components/ui/` with:

## Button
`variant`: `primary` (bg-accent / text-accent-fg, hover bg-accent-strong), `secondary` (bg-surface-2, border-border, hover bg-surface-3), `ghost` (transparent, hover bg-surface-2), `danger` (bg-danger/10 text-danger, hover bg-danger text-white). `size`: `sm` (h-9), `md` (h-11 / 44px — default, touch), `lg` (h-14). Props: `loading` (shows spinner, disables), `icon`, `iconRight`, `fullWidth`. Radius `rounded-md`. Transition `var(--dur) var(--ease)`. Pressed state: `active:scale-[0.98]`. Disabled: `opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed`.

## IconButton
Square (h-11 w-11 default), `rounded-md`, same variants, requires `aria-label`.

## Card
`surface-1` bg, `rounded-lg`, `--shadow-card`, optional `1px` hairline `border-border`. Props: `as`, `interactive` (adds hover lift `-translate-y-0.5` + `--shadow-pop`), `padding` (`none|sm|md|lg`).

## Input / Textarea
`bg-surface-2`, `rounded-md`, `ring-1 ring-border`, `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-accent`, `text` color, `placeholder:text-faint`, min-h 44px. Support leading icon slot (used by the library search). Textarea min-h 100px. Include a `Label` and optional `hint`/`error` sub-elements.

## Chip / Tag
`rounded-full`, sizes sm/md. `variant`: `neutral` (bg-surface-2 text-muted), `accent` (bg-accent/15 text-accent), `selected` (bg-accent text-accent-fg). Optional `onRemove` (renders an X, used by the tag editor) and `onClick` (used by filters).

## Feedback states
- `Spinner` (the existing `animate-spin` ring, tokenized: `border-border border-t-accent`).
- `Skeleton` (shimmer block on `surface-2`) — used by loading states instead of a bare spinner where a layout is known.
- `EmptyState` (icon slot + title + description + optional action) — replaces the plain grey "No videos yet" box.

## Acceptance criteria
- All primitives live under `src/components/ui/`, are typed, and use **only** F1 tokens (no raw `zinc-*`/hex).
- Button covers all 4 variants × 3 sizes, loading + disabled states, and meets ≥44px touch height at `md`.
- At least the Videos library page is migrated to use `Button`, `Input`, `Chip`, `Spinner`, and `EmptyState` as the reference integration (proves the API).
- Every interactive primitive shows the F1 focus ring on keyboard focus and an `active:` pressed state.
- No visual regression vs. intent; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# S1 · Home dashboard redesign

`src/app/page.tsx` is three flat colored blocks (green/blue/yellow) — the clearest "default Tailwind" tell in the app. It's the first thing seen and sets zero tone. Rebuild it as a confident, glanceable home that both greets and gets you moving.

## Direction
Shift from "3 colored buttons" to a **dashboard with a hero + a deck of entry cards + a live glance strip**.

1. **Hero.** Large display wordmark (F3 lockup) + one-line value prop. Set on `bg-base` with a subtle radial accent glow behind the mark (`--accent-glow`, very low opacity, no hard edges). Restrained — the mark and one CTA carry it.
2. **Primary CTA.** One loud primary `Button` — "Start a workout" → `/videos` (the main job). Timer/History are secondary.
3. **Entry cards (the "deck").** Replace the 3 solid color blocks with 3 `Card`s (F2, `interactive`), each with: a monochrome line icon, a title, a one-line description, and a quiet accent affordance on hover (icon tints `--accent`, card lifts). **Do not** color-code them green/blue/yellow — they share the neutral surface; the accent appears only on hover/focus. This kills the arbitrary-color problem.
4. **Glance strip (optional if data is cheap).** A thin row of 2–3 stat tiles — e.g. "X videos in your deck", "last workout Nd ago", "current streak". Pull from existing `/api/videos` and `/api/workout-logs`. If a stat has no data, show an inviting zero-state ("Add your first video") rather than "0".
5. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for the glow/hover.

## Acceptance criteria
- Home no longer uses solid green/blue/yellow blocks; entry cards use neutral surfaces with accent only on hover/focus.
- Hero wordmark uses the F3 lockup and display type scale; radial accent glow is subtle (no banding/hard edge).
- One clearly-dominant primary CTA routes to `/videos`; Timer/History are visibly secondary.
- Entry cards use the F2 `Card` primitive and are keyboard-focusable with the F1 ring.
- Layout is balanced on iPad landscape (~1024–1180px) and reflows cleanly to a single column on phones.

userStories.description:
# S2 · Video Library + VideoCard redesign

Files: `src/app/videos/page.tsx`, `src/components/VideoCard.tsx`. The library is functional but bland: low-contrast grey tag pills, a crude inline "Yes/No" text delete confirm on every card, a bare spinner while loading, and a plain grey empty box. This is the app's home base — make browsing "your deck" feel good.

## Library page
- Rebuild header/search/filters using F2 primitives (`Input` with leading search icon, filter `Chip`s, `Button`). Keep the debounced search and tag-filter logic exactly as-is.
- **Loading:** replace the bare centered spinner with a **skeleton grid** (F2 `Skeleton` cards matching the real grid) so layout doesn't jump.
- **Empty states:** use F2 `EmptyState` — a friendly icon, "Your deck is empty" / filtered variant "No cards match those filters", and a primary action. No more plain grey box.
- Result count + active-filter summary set in `text-muted` / `.text-label` eyebrow style.
- Grid: keep responsive columns; increase gap to breathe (24px), align to the token radii.

## VideoCard (the "card in your deck")
- Use F2 `Card interactive`. Thumbnail keeps 16:9; on hover, a **play affordance** scales in over a darken gradient (not a flat 40% black wash) with the play glyph in a circular accent chip.
- Provider badge (Vimeo/YouTube): move to a small, legible pill using tokens; show for both providers, not just Vimeo, so the source is always clear.
- Title: `h3` weight, hover tint `--accent`. Tags: F2 `Chip neutral` (raise contrast off the current `text-zinc-400`).
- **Fix the delete UX:** replace the inline "Yes/No" text buttons with a small confirm — either a `danger` icon-button that morphs into a compact "Delete? ✓ ✕" inline control with clear affordances, or a lightweight popover/menu. Deleting shows a spinner on the confirm control and disables it. Keep the optimistic `onDelete` behavior.
- Primary "Play" action stays prominent; Edit is a secondary IconButton.

## Acceptance criteria
- Library uses F2 `Input`, `Chip`, `Button`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`; search/filter behavior unchanged.
- Loading shows a skeleton grid (no layout shift when content arrives).
- VideoCard uses `Card interactive`; hover reveals a gradient + accent play chip (not a flat black overlay).
- Delete confirm is a clear, non-crude affordance with loading + cancel; provider badge shows for both YouTube and Vimeo.
- Tag/threshold contrast meets AA on the card surface; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# S3 · Workout session redesign — the cockpit

File: `src/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx` (+ `ExerciseCueOverlay.tsx`, `CueEditor.tsx`). This is the flagship screen — where you actually work out. It's functional but developer-y: a raw `stateColor` status **dot + `capitalize` state word**, a dense right rail stacking timer/controls/log/auto-extract/cue-list/editor with equal weight, and no glanceability hierarchy for someone looking from across the room.

## Direction: make it a cockpit with a clear hierarchy
1. **Player leads.** Full-width video in the left column, `rounded-lg`, generous.
2. **Instrument panel (right rail), reordered by glance priority:**
   - **Elapsed / duration** as the hero of the rail — bump numerals to the display scale (`Geist Mono tabular-nums`, ~`text-6xl`), `text-muted` label above. This is the thing you glance at.
   - **Replace the raw state dot + capitalized word** with a proper status pill: `Playing` → accent, `Paused` → `--paused` amber, `Ended` → `--danger`, `Loading` → muted. Rounded pill with a soft dot, not the current dev-console look.
   - **Transport controls** as large primary/secondary buttons (F2): Play/Pause primary, Restart secondary IconButton. Big enough to hit mid-workout.
   - **Log Workout** — keep, but style as a distinct secondary action (not competing blue); success state morphs in place ("Logged ✓") using accent, error in `--danger` below.
   - **Auto-extract**, **cue list**, **cue editor** — demote into a collapsible/secondary zone so they don't crowd the live controls. Consider a lightweight tab or accordion: "Cues" vs "Edit".
3. **Active cue overlay:** ensure the active exercise cue is unmissable during playback — large, high-contrast, animates in on change (hand the motion spec to M1). The cue list highlights the active row (keep existing logic).
4. Preserve all existing behavior: cue syncing, seek-on-tap, workout logging, provider switching (YouTube/Vimeo), the elapsed/duration data.

## Acceptance criteria
- The raw status dot + `capitalize` word is replaced by a semantic status pill (accent/amber/danger/muted).
- Elapsed time is the visual hero of the right rail at display-scale tabular numerals.
- Transport + Log actions use F2 buttons with clear primary/secondary hierarchy; cue-editing tools are visually demoted (collapsible/tabbed), not stacked with equal weight.
- Active cue is prominent and legible from a distance; existing cue-sync and seek behavior unchanged.
- Works on iPad landscape (two-column) and stacks cleanly on narrow widths; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# S4 · Interval Timer screen — the instrument

File: `src/app/timer/page.tsx` is a **one-line stub** ("Configure and start your interval timer here.") yet the timer is a core feature in the spec. This ticket designs and builds the timer **UI** — the most glanceable screen in the product.

> Scope note: focus is the UI + interaction design and a working front-end timer loop sufficient to demo it (work/rest/rounds countdown with transitions). Deep preset persistence to the DB can be a fast-follow if it balloons; wire to existing endpoints if present, otherwise keep presets client-side and note the follow-up.

## Direction: a giant, unmissable countdown
1. **Hero countdown.** The remaining seconds fill the viewport — `display-hero` numerals (`clamp(4rem,18vw,11rem)`, Geist Mono tabular-nums), centered. Readable across a room. Under it: current phase label ("WORK" / "REST" / "GET READY") in `.text-label` scale, and "Round 3 / 8".
2. **Phase = color, by meaning.** WORK background/ring uses `--work` (green), REST uses `--rest` (cyan/blue), the final countdown seconds pulse. The whole screen's accent shifts with the phase so a glance tells you what to do. Paused dims to `--paused`.
3. **Progress ring.** A large circular SVG progress ring around/behind the number depleting over the interval; plus a thin segmented bar showing all rounds and where you are.
4. **Count-in.** A "3 · 2 · 1 · GO" count-in before the first work interval (motion + optional beep via the existing `useAudio` hook / `src/lib/audio.ts`).
5. **Controls.** Big Start/Pause primary, Reset secondary, Skip-interval tertiary. ≥56px targets — you tap these sweaty.
6. **Config panel.** Before starting: simple controls to set work sec / rest sec / rounds, and a row of **preset chips** ("Tabata 20/10×8", "EMOM", "30/30") that populate the config. Use F2 primitives. Presets can be a static seed list to start.
7. **Audio + wake lock.** Beep on transitions (reuse audio lib); request a screen Wake Lock while running so the iPad doesn't sleep mid-workout (progressive-enhancement, guard for unsupported).

## Acceptance criteria
- Timer page renders a full instrument, not a stub: giant countdown, phase label, round indicator, progress ring, controls, and a config/preset panel.
- A configured work/rest/rounds sequence runs: counts down, transitions phases with color change + beep, handles pause/reset/skip.
- Phase color follows meaning (work=green, rest=cyan, paused=amber); final seconds pulse.
- Count-in plays before the first interval; all motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Numerals are legible at arm's length on iPad landscape; controls are ≥56px; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# S5 · Workout History screen — activity view

File: `src/app/history/page.tsx` is a **one-line stub** ("Your completed workouts will be tracked here."). Workout logs are already written by the session screen via `POST /api/workout-logs`. Design and build the UI that makes that data feel rewarding to return to.

## Direction: motivation through a glanceable activity view
1. **Summary header (glance tiles).** A row of stat `Card`s: current streak (🔥), workouts this week, total workouts, total time. Big display numerals, `.text-label` captions. These are the reward — make them the first thing seen.
2. **Consistency heatmap / streak.** A GitHub-style contribution grid (last ~12 weeks) or a week-strip of day dots, filled with `--accent` intensity by activity. Communicates the streak at a glance and pulls people back.
3. **Activity feed.** Reverse-chronological list grouped by day ("Today", "Yesterday", "Mon Jul 14"). Each row: the video thumbnail/title worked out to, duration (formatted mm:ss / h m), and time of day. Rows link back to the video. Use F2 `Card`/list styling.
4. **Empty state.** F2 `EmptyState` — encouraging, not empty-feeling: "No workouts logged yet — finish one to start your streak," with a CTA to `/videos`.
5. Fetch from `GET /api/workout-logs` (confirm/extend the route returns joined video info + timestamps; if it doesn't, add the minimal read needed — this is a read-only addition, still within UI scope).

## Acceptance criteria
- History renders summary stat tiles, a streak/consistency visual, and a grouped activity feed — not a stub.
- Feed groups by day with human labels, shows video + duration + time, and links back to the source video.
- Streak/heatmap accurately reflects logged days and uses accent-intensity, respecting reduced-motion.
- Empty state is encouraging and routes to `/videos`.
- Durations use the shared `formatTime` helper; layout works on iPad landscape and phones; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# S6 · Add/Edit Video form redesign

Files: `src/app/videos/new/page.tsx`, `src/app/videos/[id]/edit/page.tsx`. The add form is the most thought-through screen already (provider toggle, debounced URL fetch, live preview, tag chips with suggestions). Refine it onto the F2 primitives and tighten a few rough edges; bring the edit page to visual parity.

## Do
- Migrate all inputs/labels/buttons/chips to F2 primitives; remove the repeated inline `min-h-[44px]`/ring class strings.
- **Provider toggle:** turn into a clean segmented control on `surface-2` with an animated selected pill (`--accent`) sliding between YouTube/Vimeo (respect reduced-motion).
- **Live preview:** when info is fetching, show a `Skeleton` in the 16:9 preview box instead of only the "Fetching…" text; when loaded, show the provider pill + title over a subtle gradient. Keep the existing fetch/fallback logic.
- **Tag editor:** keep behavior (Enter/comma to add, Backspace to remove, suggestions, existing-tags). Restyle chips via F2 `Chip` with `onRemove`; make the input container's focus ring match F1.
- **Error/validation:** error block uses `--danger` tokens; disable submit until valid (already computed via `canSubmit`) with a clear reason hint.
- Bring `videos/[id]/edit/page.tsx` to the same look and primitives (verify it matches; if it diverges from `new`, align it).

## Acceptance criteria
- Both new and edit forms use F2 primitives exclusively (no inline ring/min-h magic strings).
- Provider selection is an animated segmented control; preview shows a skeleton while fetching.
- Tag add/remove/suggest behavior is unchanged and restyled via F2 `Chip`.
- Errors use `--danger`; submit stays disabled until valid; both pages are visually consistent; `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# M1 · Motion & micro-interaction system pass

The app has almost no motion beyond `transition-colors` and a spinner. A fitness product should feel alive and responsive. Add a small, coherent motion language using the F1 tokens (`--dur*`, `--ease`). **Motion communicates state; it never just decorates.** Everything gated behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.

## Interactions to add (all using `--ease`)
- **Buttons/cards:** press `active:scale-[0.98]`; interactive cards lift on hover (`-translate-y-0.5` + shadow-pop). (Mostly from F2 — verify consistency here.)
- **Active exercise cue (session):** on cue change, the overlay does a quick scale-up + fade (from ~0.96→1, `--dur`), so a new exercise visibly "snaps" in. This is the signature moment.
- **Timer (S4):** the progress ring depletes smoothly; final 3 seconds pulse the numerals; the work→rest transition cross-fades the phase color across the screen; the count-in "3·2·1·GO" scales each digit.
- **Route/tab transitions:** subtle fade/slide-up (8px) on page content mount; the nav active indicator slides between items (shared-layout style).
- **Toasts/success:** the "Workout Logged ✓" state morphs in place rather than snapping.
- **Skeletons:** a slow shimmer sweep on loading placeholders.
- **List/grid mount:** optional light stagger (≤40ms step, capped) when the video grid first renders — keep it tasteful, no long cascades.

## Guardrails
- Prefer CSS transitions/`@keyframes` and existing React state; only reach for a library if truly needed (call it out first — default to none).
- No animation longer than `--dur-slow` (320ms) for UI feedback; nothing blocks input.
- Full `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` path: transforms/opacity animations disabled, state still changes instantly and legibly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Cue-change, timer phase/pulse/count-in, nav indicator slide, page mount fade, and success-morph are all implemented with token timings.
- Every animation has a reduced-motion fallback that conveys the same state without movement.
- No jank on iPad (transform/opacity only; no layout-thrash animations); `pnpm build` passes.

userStories.description:
# A1 · Accessibility, contrast & iPad/responsive hardening

**Closeout gate — run last, after the screens land.** "Impeccable" isn't just pretty; it's legible, operable, and correct on the real device. Sweep the redesigned app for a11y, contrast, and iPad/responsive correctness.

## Fix / verify
1. **Remove the zoom lock.** `src/app/layout.tsx` sets `maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false` — this blocks pinch-zoom and is an accessibility failure. Remove `maximumScale`/`userScalable` (keep `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`).
2. **Contrast (AA).** Audit all text/background pairs against the F1 tokens. `--text-muted` on `surface-1/2` must clear 4.5:1 for body / 3:1 for large; never use `--text-faint` for essential text. Fix any offenders (the old `text-zinc-500` hints were borderline).
3. **Focus visible everywhere.** Every interactive element shows the F1 focus ring; verify custom controls (segmented toggle, filter chips, cue rows, card overlays) are reachable and operable by keyboard, in a logical tab order.
4. **Semantics & labels.** Icon-only buttons have `aria-label`; the timer exposes state to assistive tech (`aria-live` polite for phase/round changes, not every tick); status pill has a text label, not color-only; form inputs keep associated `<label>`s.
5. **Touch targets.** All primary controls ≥44px; timer transport ≥56px (S4).
6. **Responsive matrix.** Verify each screen at: iPad landscape (1180×820) and portrait (820×1180), a 390px phone, and a 1440px desktop. Two-column layouts (session, add-form) collapse cleanly; the timer countdown never clips; the video grid reflows; nav stays usable. No horizontal scroll at any breakpoint.
7. **Motion safety.** Confirm the M1 reduced-motion paths actually engage under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
8. **Images.** All `next/image` thumbnails have meaningful `alt`; broken-thumbnail fallback (already present) still reads well.

## Acceptance criteria
- Zoom lock removed; pinch-zoom works on iOS Safari.
- No essential text/icon fails AA against its background (spot-check the key pairs and list them in the ticket comments).
- Full keyboard operability with visible focus on every screen; icon-only controls labeled; timer announces phase changes via `aria-live`.
- Each screen verified at the four breakpoints above with no clipping or horizontal scroll.
- Reduced-motion fully disables non-essential animation; `pnpm build` + `pnpm lint` pass.

userStories.description:
# F3 · Brand identity + Navigation redesign

The brand is currently just the word "WorkoutDeck" with "Workout" tinted green — no mark, no personality. The nav (`src/components/Navigation.tsx`) is a plain sticky bar. Give the product a real identity and a nav that recedes but orients.

## Logomark
Design a compact SVG mark evoking the "deck" metaphor — a small stack of offset cards / a play-triangle fused with a stacked-cards silhouette, rendered in `--accent`. Ships as an inline React component `src/components/ui/Logo.tsx` (mark + optional wordmark lockup). Must read clearly at 24px (nav) and 40px+ (home hero). Provide `size` and `withWordmark` props.

## Wordmark
Set "WorkoutDeck" in the display weight (tracking-tight, 700/800). Drop the two-tone green/white split in favor of a single confident treatment: white wordmark + accent logomark, OR the accent reserved for a single glyph (e.g. the "D" or the mark) — pick the cleaner of the two and use it everywhere consistently.

## Navigation
- Background `surface-1/80` with `backdrop-blur`, bottom hairline `border-border`. Height 64px.
- Left: Logo (mark + wordmark, links home).
- Right: nav links. Active link = `bg-accent/12 text-accent` with a 2px accent underline or left-edge indicator (not a full solid green fill — that's too loud for chrome). Inactive = `text-muted hover:text-white hover:bg-surface-2`. Keep ≥44px targets.
- **iPad-first:** the app is used in landscape on iPad. Ensure the bar is comfortable at 768–1180px; consider promoting nav labels with small inline icons (video / timer / history) for faster glance recognition. Icons come from the existing inline-SVG pattern in the repo.
- Add active-link motion: the underline/indicator slides between items (respect reduced-motion).

## Acceptance criteria
- `Logo.tsx` renders a legible custom mark at 24px and 40px, using `--accent`.
- Nav uses tokens only, shows a clear but quiet active state (not a solid green button), and preserves all four routes.
- Wordmark treatment is unified and used in both nav and home hero.
- Touch targets ≥44px; keyboard focus rings present; `pnpm build` passes.

epicTitle: "The Deck" — WorkoutDeck UI Overhaul & Design System
epicDescription:
# "The Deck" — WorkoutDeck UI Overhaul

## Why this epic exists

WorkoutDeck works, but it looks like un-opinionated default Tailwind: flat `#0a0a0a` canvas, one accent color arbitrarily assigned per nav item (green/blue/yellow), no design tokens, inconsistent radii, developer-y details (a raw status dot + `capitalize` state string), and **two core screens — Timer and History — are literal one-line stubs.** The product is a fitness instrument you glance at from across a room on an iPad mid-workout. It should feel like premium athletic hardware, not a CRUD admin panel.

This epic replaces the incumbent generic look with a committed visual world and the token/component foundation to keep it consistent. It does **not** change product truth, data model, routes, or copy meaning — it's a visual + interaction uplift plus building out the two stub screens' UI.

> Implementation note: these tickets are written to be implemented by another engineer (SOL). Every value is explicit — hex codes, type scale, radii, motion specs — so there is no guesswork. Ticket **F1 (design tokens)** and **F2 (UI primitives)** are the foundation; land them first, then everything else consumes them.

## The POV: "The Deck" — a high-energy athletic control surface

Metaphor: the name is WorkoutDeck. Lean into it — each video is a **card in your deck**; the timer is the **instrument**; the session screen is the **cockpit**. Calm, dark, tactile surfaces with one confident signal color for energy/GO, big glanceable numerals, and purposeful motion. Restraint everywhere except the numbers and the primary action, which are loud on purpose.

Design principles:
1. **Glanceable first.** iPad, landscape, arm's length, possibly sweaty. Numbers and the current action must read in <0.5s. Big tabular numerals, high contrast, generous hit targets.
2. **One signal color, with meaning.** Green = GO/active/energy. Everything else is structure (slate/graphite). Color is assigned by *meaning* (work vs rest vs paused vs destructive), never decoratively per-feature.
3. **Tactile, layered surfaces.** Real elevation via layered greys + hairline top-highlight, not flat panels. Consistent radii.
4. **Motion with purpose.** Cue changes, the count-in, the work→rest flip, tab transitions — motion communicates state, never decorates. Always honor `prefers-reduced-motion`.
5. **Quiet chrome, loud content.** Nav and controls recede; the video, the timer, the active cue lead.

## Committed design tokens (source of truth — implemented in F1)

### Color — layered dark
```
--bg-base:        #0B0C0E   /* app canvas, slightly cool near-black */
--surface-1:      #131518   /* cards, panels */
--surface-2:      #1B1E22   /* inputs, raised controls */
--surface-3:      #23272C   /* hover / pressed surface */
--border:         #2A2F36   /* hairline */
--border-strong:  #3A4048   /* focused / emphasized edges */

--text:           #F2F4F5   /* primary */
--text-muted:     #A7B0B8   /* secondary — AA on surface-1/2 */
--text-faint:     #6B747C   /* tertiary / disabled-ish, non-essential only */

--accent:         #38E07B   /* brand signal: GO / active / energy */
--accent-strong:  #16C060   /* pressed/hover accent */
--accent-fg:      #05210F   /* near-black text ON accent (AA) */
--accent-glow:    rgba(56,224,123,0.35)  /* focus ring / halo */

/* Semantic (assign by meaning, not feature) */
--work:  #38E07B   /* work interval = GO (same as accent) */
--rest:  #38BDF8   /* rest interval = cool/recover */
--paused:#FBBF24   /* paused / warning */
--danger:#F4515B   /* destructive / ended */
```
Replace every raw `zinc-*`, `green-600`, `blue-600`, `yellow-500`, `red-600` in the codebase with these tokens (exposed as Tailwind theme colors via `@theme inline`, e.g. `bg-surface-1`, `text-muted`, `bg-accent text-accent-fg`).

### Typography
- Body/UI: keep **Geist Sans**. Numerals/timers: keep **Geist Mono** with `tabular-nums`.
- Wordmark + big display: a strong geometric/grotesk display weight (Geist at 700/800 with `tracking-tight` is acceptable if adding a font is undesirable).
- Scale (use CSS custom props / Tailwind text tokens):
  `display-hero clamp(4rem,18vw,11rem)/0.95 tracking-[-0.03em]` (timer + session numerals) ·
  `display-xl 2.5rem/1.05 -0.02em` · `h1 2rem/1.1` · `h2 1.5rem/1.15` · `h3 1.25rem` ·
  `body 1rem/1.5` · `small 0.875rem` · `xs 0.75rem` ·
  `label 0.8125rem, uppercase, tracking-[0.06em], text-muted` (section eyebrows).

### Radius / elevation / motion
```
--r-sm: 8px   --r-md: 12px   --r-lg: 16px   --r-xl: 20px   --r-full: 9999px
  Cards/panels → r-lg · Buttons/inputs → r-md · Chips/pills → r-full

--shadow-card: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.04) inset, 0 12px 32px -16px rgba(0,0,0,0.7)
--shadow-pop:  0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05) inset, 0 20px 50px -20px rgba(0,0,0,0.8)

--dur-fast: 120ms  --dur: 200ms  --dur-slow: 320ms
--ease: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)   /* confident, slightly springy */
```
All motion wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.

## Scope / non-goals
- **In scope:** visual system, tokens, reusable primitives, per-screen redesign, building out the Timer & History screen *UI*, motion, accessibility/contrast, iPad/responsive polish.
- **Out of scope:** data model changes, API changes, new product features beyond what the spec already defines (Timer & History are already in the spec — we're designing their UI). Timer *engine* logic beyond what's needed to demo the UI can be a follow-up if it grows large.
- **Preserve:** all routes, copy meaning, functionality, the dark theme direction, YouTube/Vimeo provider behavior.

## Suggested landing order
F1 tokens → F2 primitives → F3 brand+nav → then screens (home, library+card, session, timer, history, add/edit form) in parallel → M1 motion pass → A1 accessibility/iPad hardening as the closeout gate.
